mbm-1901.clue: The first row has room for a rocket.
mbm-1901.quote: Our cinema lets kids draw spaceships before the matinee. I kept my nephew's first one in the ticket envelope. It has a popcorn machine on every deck.

mbm-1902.clue: I keep a hotel key for an imaginary room.
mbm-1902.quote: I got a chipped wooden key tag at a sale and gave it to the night porter in my story. If a chapter sticks, I turn the tag over and picture who's at his desk.

mbm-1903.clue: My blanket knows where the puddles were.
mbm-1903.quote: I traced our old playground into patchwork. Mum put blue stitches exactly where our coats used to get soaked. Looking at it, I can still feel the biggest puddle coming over my socks.

mbm-1904.clue: I've got a spoon with no matching set.
mbm-1904.quote: I choose one stray spoon from the market whenever my sister visits. Sunday dessert is a whole roomful of different patterns. She can remember where every one came from.

mbm-1905.clue: I save the silver ribbon for the last track.
mbm-1905.quote: My friend and I tied strips of gift ribbon to our wrists for a night out. When the lights went blue, the ribbons drew two spinning circles in the dark. We still have them in our record sleeves.

mbm-1906.clue: The astronaut on my screen wears slippers.
mbm-1906.quote: I drew my own little space game for my dad. The astronaut's boots looked so much like his slippers that I put a rocking chair on the moon. Dad says it's the only sensible destination.

mbm-1907.clue: My password is a musical joke.
mbm-1907.quote: I programmed a tiny piano for my cousin. If she plays our doorbell tune, a pixel dog runs to the edge of the screen. The real dog barks from under the desk.

mbm-1908.clue: I trimmed the corners like envelopes.
mbm-1908.quote: My dad worked the mail route for years. I pieced a quilt of envelopes from his old uniform shirts. He recognized the postbox red before I unfolded the blue side.

mbm-1909.clue: I can keep a conversation going with three scarves.
mbm-1909.quote: I matched my juggling scarves to traffic lights. When the red one floats up, my niece pauses her story. It took her half an hour to tell me one excellent joke.

mbm-1910.clue: I don't throw out worn record sleeves.
mbm-1910.quote: I cut little dark stars from a spare sleeve and pinned them to my dance shirt. When the DJ played that record, my friend pointed from the cover to my collar. Best request I never had to make.

mbm-1911.clue: There's a little wooden boat on the roof.
mbm-1911.quote: I teach my nephew the rules with a board game we made. He parked his boat on top of the hotel and invented a flood. I wrote his rule in the lid. We're on our third edition.

mbm-1912.clue: The boat crew have their own medal.
mbm-1912.quote: When I finally crossed the wake on one ski, my friends handed me a washer threaded on a shoelace. I stamped their names on the back. There wouldn't have been any tricks without a boat.

mbm-1913.clue: I can recognize that robin by one white toe.
mbm-1913.quote: A robin liked to perch on the handle of our spade. I drew it from the kitchen all spring before noticing the one pale claw. Now even my roughest sketch looks like our particular bird.

mbm-1914.clue: One star on the blanket has a handle.
mbm-1914.quote: The first piece I cut for my quilt was too close to an old shirt cuff. I left its buttonhole on the star. My niece hooks a finger through it when she drags the quilt to the couch.

mbm-1915.clue: My favorite work is smaller than its label.
mbm-1915.quote: A miniature plum sat beside a panel several times its size. I made a little frame with my fingers and peered at one painted blossom on its side. I forgot to read the label until my third visit.

mbm-1916.clue: I taught the curtains a new trick.
mbm-1916.quote: I practiced juggling on our little stage before rehearsal. One ball caught in the velvet folds. At my bow the curtain opened and dropped the missing ball into my hands. Nobody believed it was an accident.

mbm-1917.clue: My vase has a crooked little belt.
mbm-1917.quote: The clay sagged halfway through throwing it. I added a ribbon of clay around the waist and stamped a buckle. My sister puts daisies in it with the buckle turned toward the door.

mbm-1918.clue: The fair photographer kept the best berry.
mbm-1918.quote: My first berry tart burst onto my nose before the eating contest had begun. The photographer pointed. I left the spot there until the last plate, just for a good before-and-after.

mbm-1919.clue: I quilted a map of the kitchen floor.
mbm-1919.quote: We used to hop across the cracked tiles when we were small. I stitched each crack into the patchwork in gold. My sister saw it and did the whole route with two fingers.

mbm-1920.clue: I had to juggle sideways for that train.
mbm-1920.quote: The little waiting room was barely wider than my shoulders. A stuck train meant an hour with three scarves and a very patient stationmaster. When the train came, he asked me to show him the sideways catch once more.

mbm-1921.clue: I've got a route named after a missing glove.
mbm-1921.quote: I found a striped glove on my morning run and followed paper notices back to its owner. She gave me a new route past her favorite orange trees. I still call it the Glove Loop.

mbm-1922.clue: My sister gives the chalkboard eyes.
mbm-1922.quote: At the gym I cross off each completed set. My sister turns the chalk marks into a little animal at the end. I once did an extra set so her dachshund could have four legs.

mbm-1923.clue: The program grew a whisker overnight.
mbm-1923.quote: I taught my pixel cat to stretch every hour. A drawing error left one whisker behind each time. By morning the screen was full of fine white rain. I saved that version.

mbm-1924.clue: I once paddled a full mile for a sandwich swap.
mbm-1924.quote: My friend left my mustard sandwich in his canoe and I had his jam. We met halfway across the lake and made the exchange with two outstretched paddles and a lot of laughing.

mbm-1925.clue: The blue piece has to take the scenic route.
mbm-1925.quote: When our board wore out along one edge, Dad glued on a bit of a bus map. Now there's an optional detour past three real bus stops. It adds two turns and always gets my vote.
